edges.notes: Kata Containers targets Linux hosts for KVM/QEMU-class lightweight VM sandboxes around OCI workloads per upstream documentation.
Provides an OCI-compatible runtime path for executing bundles with VM-level isolation per project documentation.
Documented Kubernetes integration patterns (e.g., RuntimeClass) for selecting VM-isolated runtimes on nodes.
Commonly composed with containerd/CRI stacks as the low-level VM-backed runtime alternative to default runc-class runtimes.
QEMU is used in typical Linux VM sandbox paths; QEMU is the VMM component, Kata is the container runtime integration layer.
KVM accelerates guest VMs on Linux nodes; KVM is the kernel API, Kata composes it for OCI execution.
Substitutable low-level isolation boundary for OCI bundles: namespace-isolated runc vs VM-backed Kata—different threat models.
Different isolation mechanisms for OCI bundles: VM-backed Kata vs gVisor userspace syscall interposition (not equivalent threat models).
